subject: Demo recap + proposed pilot handshake: Montclair systems evaluation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Demo recap + proposed pilot handshake: Montclair systems evaluation

Hi Lena / Devon — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed small-scale pilot to validate latency, relevance, and integration effort.

TL;DR: We recommend a 4-week evaluation (2-week integration + 2-week evaluation window) scoped to the Search & Triage workflow you showed. Goal: demonstrate 80th percentile latency <= 350ms, precision uplift of triage suggestions by +15% on sample set, and operational readiness (end-to-end deployment, monitoring, and runbook).

Background + ask:
- Demo highlights: connector to your S3 event store, streaming responses for multi-turn triage, and built-in prefix caching that reduced token costs in our test harness.
- What we need from you to start: sample query set (10k anonymized queries), representative documents/KB (S3 location or Share), and a point-of-contact for infra (network/VPC) and security (SOC2 evidence).

Proposed pilot plan (outline attached: montclair-eval-outline.pdf):
1) Week 0 (kickoff, day 1): alignment call, NDA/MCF check, access list + IP allowlist, HubSpot record created: HUBSPOT-34567.
2) Week 1–2 (integration): credentials exchange, connector setup, lightweight model tuning (no weights transfer), basic metrics plumbing (latency, token counts, success error rates). Owners: Marcus (AM), Jordan (Solutions).
3) Week 3–4 (evaluation window): run 10k queries through pipeline, produce quantitative report vs baseline, weekly checkpoints, final exec sync. Owners: Montclair analytics lead + Marissa (CS).
4) Acceptance criteria: latency SLO met (80th <= 350ms), relevance delta >= +15% vs baseline labeled set, and reproducible logs + dashboard.

Budget and licensing: For this pilot we can provide a time-limited credit model (hosted API) and a small reserved credit for burst testing. If you need a dedicated pool or private deployment we'll scope separately.

Next steps (proposed):
- Please confirm sample data availability and who will be the infra/security POC by EOD Friday.
- If agreed, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff next Monday to assign accounts, share runbook, and open access.

Attachments: montclair-eval-outline.pdf (PDF), montclair-kpis.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0139

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. I looped in Devon (ops) and procurement for visibility. A few clarifying Qs before we commit to a kickoff: 

1) Data: we can produce a 10k anonymized query sample but it will take 3–4 business days to scrub and approve. Is that timeline acceptable?
2) Security: Montclair needs to confirm SOC2 scope — can you send the specific artifacts (e.g., auditor contact or package) you typically share for pilots?
3) Metrics: the +15% relevance uplift — is that measured on top-N suggestions accuracy or on final triage decision accuracy? Please be explicit in the report so our analytics team can mirror the calculation.

If the scrub takes longer, can we start Week 1 with a synthetic dataset so integration work doesn't stall? Also: procurement asked for an itemized pilot estimate (even if covered by credit) so they have the cost baseline.

I'll aim to get the POC resource names to you by Friday.

Best,
Lena
Director, Search & Insights | Montclair Systems

Hi Lena — great questions, answers inline below.

1) Data scrub: 3–4 business days is fine. Starting with synthetic data for Week 1 integration is exactly what we recommend — it keeps momentum while you finalize scrub approval. We’ll provide a small synthetic pack that mirrors your cardinality and token distributions.

2) Security artifacts: attached sample SOC2 summary + auditor contact (PDF) and a concise pilot checklist we use in early engagements. For pilots we typically share a redacted auditor summary and a SOC2 assertion letter; anything else you require we can discuss with Security & Legal.

3) Metrics clarity: the +15% uplift refers to top-3 suggestion precision measured against your labeled triage decisions (i.e., if the model’s top-3 contains the correct triage label). We will include both top-1 and top-3 metrics in the final report and provide the calculation script. Metric definition will be included in montclair-kpis.xlsx.

Procurement note: we’ll produce an itemized pilot estimate for your finance/procurement contact. For clarity — the pilot is typically zero-cost when run within our hosted evaluation credits; the estimate reflects list pricing so procurement has a reference.

Proposed kickoff slots (PST): Monday 10:00–10:30 or Monday 14:00–14:30. Which works for your team?

Action items for this thread:
- Marcus: share synthetic data pack + SOC2 summary (attached).
- Montclair: confirm POC names and procurement contact by Friday.
- Marissa: will prepare the monitoring dashboard template and runbook.
- Jordan: will own connector/auth setup and will follow up with network ranges.

Attachments: sample-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF), synthetic-data-pack.zip (ZIP), montclair-kpis.xlsx (XLSX)

Regards,
Marcus
